item.title: Lock and ___
item.description: A locked, indestructible safe with no key that has a dangerous hallucinogenic and transformative effect on those who stay too close for too long.
item.content:encoded:
I've posted this one before and intended to approach people directly for reviews, but I've been busy and it's been well over two weeks now since the last post so I thought I'd give the forum one last shot! I have made minor alterations due to the feedback I did receive last time (not from an official reviewer but helpful feedback nonetheless).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 15 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Effect is purely proximity-based – object safely observable from a distance. 3 – 72 hours after hallucinations begin, these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made several times to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: As this is my first SCP idea I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away!

item.title: Hospital that heals you on its own.
item.description: A hospital that heals any injured or sick humans that enter, and tries it with other life and artificial items too, with mixed results.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A hospital, in a relatively populated area. Anyone who is sick, or injured, that walks in, will start to recover or heal, across the course of a few days to a few months, depending. Non-human life mutates, as if it's trying to become human, and ends up dead. Broken or damaged artificial objects 'heal' over with human biological components. 'Nurse' entities appear as body disposal, and to move immobile 'patients' to a bed. Where they come from is unknown, but they don't heal, they just don't die.

Central Narrative: On the worldbuilding side, this'll be in a relatively populated area, and may require not only fancy containment procedures, due to the hospital keeping itself looking in working order, and sending out "appointment" letters to the local area, somehow aware of illness or injury within a certain radius of it. Given its location, it may also require cooperation with a GoI, or local authorities, or some sort of group outside of the foundation. Perhaps it got discovered by two at a roughly similar time, or otherwise the foundation had it first, but then some other group (likely the GOC given they are, to my knowledge, the most able to show their faces in public, or the UIU if I put this in the states) turns up.

Experiment wise, it'll probably be a case of them trying to see how far it'll go, finding it can cure anomalous diseases (if the patient is still alive and human), and injuries, as well as things not thought fixable by modern medicine. Perhaps implication of some researcher using it for personal use, and getting into a lot of trouble for it, along with the expected D-Class abuse to see just what this thing can heal. Some stuff as well with the nurses, finding they're non-hostile, but trying to figure out where they come from, only to discover they're the patients that don't make it, put together into the nurses, and animated by unknown means.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I'd like to think the hospital itself is pretty unique, but I'd also use this as a sort of way of tying a few other SCPs together, those that are disease based, or cause funky injuries, and how the hospital tries to "fix" them. The slower time scale means that whilst telling why things are healing is impossible, observing what specifically is happening isn't. The nurses being non-hostile and non-belligerent also aids to this, since they can just put researchers in there with the D-Class to see what happens day by day.

Additional Notes: This is the first SCP I'll have ever tried to write. I've been reading for a good while, but my knowledge isn't encyclopaedic. Any ideas off of the vaguer points here would be greatly appreciated, and again I'm very sorry if this is too close to something that already exists.

item.title: The Old Lady's House / Get Out, Intruder (open to critique and/or greenlights)
item.description: It is my very first (and humble) step into submitting an idea for a SCP article.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Fairly simple. The usual "number + class + SCP + description" block, followed by logs about the discovery of the item and research led on it.

[From here: 386 words]

Elevator Pitch: House is "haunted" after the passing of its previous inhabitant; TV screen in the kitchen warns anyone who stays too long in the kitchen, then the house proceeds to kill/absorb them if the warning is ignored.

Central Narrative: A grandma who used to live alone in her small, residential street house, passes away. Since then, the house considers any human (or any large enough animal – cats are an exception) as an intruder, and proceeds to warn them through a three-step vague set of warnings displayed on the kitchen's TV set. If the warnings are ignored, the "intruder" is then killed and absorbed by the house; their remains are found in a locker somewhere in the house (or perhaps in the garden?).

Possible ramifications:

+ show block
– hide block
  • If the TV is unplugged or turned off, warnings aren't displayed yet the house kills intruders anyway.
  • People exposed to the warnings, but who left the house after the 2nd warning (therefore ignoring the 1st one), might be similarly warned by the TV set of their own home, and therefore risk getting killed in the same fashion (the "effect" "follows" them)
  • One of the logs has a D-Class almost leaving the house in time, but they trip; most of their body is outside of the house when the absorption event begins, but the house absorbs their toes, which stayed inside when the event occured
  • Cats are unaffected because the old lady gave them shelter in the house (relevance?)
  • Bringing the old lady's corpse back to the house stops the effect (would it strip away any interest from the SCP article, or (oppositely) be considered as an appropriate form of containment?)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I have absolutely no idea about what would make this idea special. I'm not very ambitious.

Additional Notes: This is an idea which appeared to me after binge-reading some entries on this website. I think I can pull off the "number + class + SCP + description" block, but I am worried about how I could build a backstory behind it. I figure the old lady could be a start, but I think I'm a bit "weak" in that area (I want it to be a bit more than just a house which kills people: why does it consider other people as "intruders"? does the old lady have a story? etc)

Thank you for your attention and thanks in advance for any input!

item.title: Abiogenesis (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science-Fiction (probably set in the Ad-Astra canon, I'm not sure yet.)

Page Layout (Optional): Classic SCP style with mission logs.

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a spatial anomaly in the outer-reaches of the solar system in the form of an Einstein–Rosen bridge (aka wormhole). On the other side, they can detect a planet. Emission spectroscopy implies that the planet may be habitable. Foundation personnel are sent through, and subsequent events shake the Foundation's view of what they think they know.

► Additional details
▼ Additional details

Central Narrative: After probes fail to return from the wormhole, the Foundation sends a manned mission through the wormhole in hopes of finding a new habitable world. The narrative follows them in the form of a series of mission logs. When they arrive on the other side, they are unable to communicate with Command. They find themselves around a rocky planet, not dissimilar to our own.

One of the crew gets in the lander to land on the planet and assess the habitability. Meanwhile, those that remained on the mothership perform scans of the solar system to check for other orbital bodies. The crew come to an astonishing revelation, the solar system doesn't look much different to our own. That's when they realise wormhole didn't send them through space, it sent them through time. Approximately 4 billion years into the past. The ground crew landed on a primordial Earth, which they've now seeded with nucleotides, nucleases, bacteria etc. The wormhole starts to become unstable and so the crew in orbit make the difficult decision to make their way back to the wormhole. It was in vain, however, as the wormhole closes and they are left in a highly elliptical orbit around the sun, completely out of fuel. Modern day Foundation find the ancient spacecraft in the modern day, and the final log of the captain, detailing on he he believes they kickstarted abiogenesis (life from non-life).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Humanity inadvertently jump started life on Earth by landing on the primordial Earth in the past. Our unknowing astronauts mediated abiogenesis - life from non-life. All of Earth's life can be traced back to a single common ancestor, created through the highly unlikely and poorly understood event of abiogenesis. This event.

Additional Notes: Any tips on how to tighten the plot would be great.

item.title: Seeking Greenlights: A Second Reflection (accounting for criticisms))
item.description: I have made modifications to the pitch after receiving helpful criticism.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.
It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.
Once in containment, SCP-XXXX does not require any sort of furniture in its containment cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), only needing a cooling system to keep it from phasing out of the room. It does need to be fed, and its meals consist of wild animals and, if a test takes an unfortunate turn, an unlucky Class-D personnel.
It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell, and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment. This aggression is seemingly nullified while SCP-XXXX is in the presence of SCP-XXXX-B.
SCP-XXXX-B is the infant born from SCP-XXXX. It resembles a humanoid infant with lighter colored skin than its parent. It shares the same invisibility as its parent, but has not yet displayed any signs of aggression.
Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.
At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.
In the months following the containment of SCP-XXXX, it is discovered to have been pregnant, and it gives birth to SCP-XXXX-B while in containment. This, followed by repeated sightings of SCP-XXXX out in the wild despite it being in containment confirms that SCP-XXXX is not an isolated anomaly, but an entire species of creatures with the same abilities.

item.title: A skull that loves to sing Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A skull that is sapient that can make sound anywhere in the world as well as hear everything that is being done in the world. The skull can also make exact imitations of sound and voices. The skull also knows languages that were wiped out and some that aren't even recorded in history. The skull can move its lower jaw but doesn't need it to make sound. The pitch of the sound made from the skull seems to be limitless.

Central Narrative: The skull was obtained from a cult that was taking skulls from people. It was sent when a police officer that was actually a foundation personnel was asked by the skull for help. On the way to a site the skull conducted a interview with a researcher at the site. Through the interviews it is revealed it has been around since 16th century and that the it became this because it saw something it shouldn't. The skull suffers a tremendous amount of mental damage as it can hear all of the suffering of the world. Singing in cafeteria however has been an emotional anchor an idea thought by the foundation to relieve it of some pain. This has worked even though only a little. The skull is going through therapy every week to find out more about its past.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook is show readers a fairly simple idea but the more you read into the story you realise the skull has a very mysterious and traumatic past through the interviews conducted during therapy sessions.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by SCP-774 as a skull that made sound. I then added hear no evil, speak no evil, see no evil concept and worked the skull's backstory around that. This my first time writing an scp so any feedback is appreciated. Also if anything isn't clear please let me know

item.title: Modern Revival of an Age-Old Industry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation finds hundreds of dead whales in the middle of the woods, with no idea how they got there. Turns out to be foul play.

Central Narrative: On an otherwise idyllic day in a sleepy small town in British Columbia, a 60-ton Right Whale materializes on top of someone's house and makes a big mess. The Foundation swoops in and covers the whole thing up. Not a big deal. Shit like this happens every day in the Foundation-verse.

Then some hikers find the remains of another whale impaled on a tree. Now the Foundation's is interested. They establish a task force to look for more dead whales in the Canadian back-country, and end up finding (literal) tons of them in various stages of decomposition. Dead whales in the treetops. Dead whales 300 kilometers inland. Dead whales embedded in the ground, or dashed out on rocks, or totally pureed as if they've been dropped from a great height. They do some cursory biological / genetic analysis on the remains. Turns out that they all come from a specific part of the Bering Sea.

Through means that I have yet to think up, the Foundation learns that the whales were teleported into the woods by poachers with anomalous hunting technology. Their intent was to beam the poor animals to a "chop shop" in the States, where they could be dissected and sold for oil and ambergris. Because their teleporters were faulty over long distances, only about 30% of the whales made it to the chop shop. The rest were randomly dispersed in the space between. When the poachers were confronted by a police patrol boat, they tried to teleport themselves the hell out of Dodge and met the same grisly fate as the other 70%.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a narrative mystery, with enough inherent wackiness to make it compelling.

Elevator Pitch: A non-corporeal entity takes random individuals' appearance throughout the places it came across. The entity existed in an unknown multi-dimensional location.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a non-corporeal entity that takes random individuals' appearance throughout the places it came across. The entity shows no signs of hostility, is capable of speech, and understands all sorts of languages. SCP-XXXX would usually gather random individuals from a universe, or different universes that are chosen by it into a massive cinematic room created by itself and would expose to those individuals all information that it wants them to know or the information that they must/want to know/learn, regardless of whether if the information that the entity exposed could lead to big consequences.

SCP-XXXX was first discovered when it was in the middle of gathering a group of peoples into its cinematic/theatre room; this time, it takes an adult form. One of the individuals it has gathered is the Foundation's researcher on his way to work. As the researcher has stayed undercover for a long period and witnessed the entity exposed the information of the Foundation to all gathered individuals.

The researcher has reported back to the Foundation from what he has seen, including each gathered individuals' reaction. This has soon resulted in the dispatching of MTF Lambda-5; however, where he is being held with the other individuals is unknown. Because the Foundation's satellite couldn't locate where it is, they've had no choice but to aboard the mission.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an entity that came across the multiverse and did not expose its true form and attempts to spill out information that're strictly forbidden not to be revealed under any circumstances.

Additional Notes: This is just a summary of the SCP; due to exceeding 400 words, I must shorten it. If you want the full, then ask me for a draft.

item.content:encoded:
Hello fellow SCP-Enthusiasts,

item.title: A Quaint Little Farm Town On Top of Several Kilometers of Ice
item.content:encoded:

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX refers to an inhabited region consisting of a small town and outlying farmland, located inland of the Transatlantic Mountains, south of the Ross Ice Shelf. Residents of SCP-XXXX refer to it as "Shackleton County." SCP-XXXX's fields can be seen to contain plants, resembling typical crops, in tilled snow, through unknown means. Residents of SCP-XXXX do not seem to suffer from discomfort or serious harm in the their cold environment, even without specialized clothing, but appear and behave typically in all other respects. Residents have been observed to use vehicles resembling large, closed-cabin snowmobiles comparable to personal automobiles and freight trucks. Residents are observed to leave the area of the "county" only once each month, when an organized group of 50-100 residents form a convoy, identifying their destination as "Erebus City." These departures are always accompanied by a blizzard causing near-total loss of visibility for Foundation observers, and attempts to track their location by other means have always failed to date. These convoys invariably return four days after their departure, similarly obscured, carrying personal and commercial goods. It is unknown where or how these items are obtained.

Central Narrative:
Central Narrative:

Containment of SCP-XXX relies heavily on Foundation sites disguised as research bases. In particular, sites on the Ross shelf are considered to be critical to the goal of maintaining containment without alerting SCP-XXXX's residents to containment efforts. Citing fears that such sites might be rendered unusable in the future if climate change causes the ice shelf to recede, a senior researcher proposes a plan under which the Foundation would become actively involved in fighting climate change. This proposal is rejected on the grounds that climate change is an element of consensus reality, and the potential threat to SCP-XXXX's containment is distant and insufficient to justify action. Convinced of the necessity of Foundation involvement in the issue, she seeks to undermine the consensus status of climate change by spreading memetic agents through public channels. While unsuccessful in creating the circumstances for Foundation intervention, this contributes to the popularity of denial movements regarding climate change, as well as dangerous containment breaches.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The use of a classic horror setting - Antarctic mountains - for a mostly-normal settlement, and the idea of a Foundation employee trying to force the Foundation into action outside its norms

Additional Notes: Honestly, this could easily become too polemical or goofy. I think it's a good basis, though.

Page Layout (Optional): Classic SCP layout; addenda will include a neutralisation proposal, interview with site-director, and a containment breach. This addenda will be presented in a novel style in the form an official document/folder (for an idea, see SCP-5859.)

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation hears reports of people becoming infected with a seemingly untreatable strain of the Bubonic Plague. MTF Beta-7 ("Maz Hatters") are deployed to control the situation. What follows is a deconstruction of the Foundations M.O: Secure, Contain, Protect.

► Additional details
▼ Additional details

Central Narrative: The SCP in question is a the corpse of a 14th century Parisian male discovered deep within the catacombs of Paris (stumbled upon by Patient-Zero, an overeager urban explorer.) Due to the anti-Semitic slur scorched into the corpse's chest, Foundation historians have theorised that the corpse was murdered due to the Christian persecution of the Jewish populace admist the onset of the Bubonic Plague.

The corpse is the cause of the outbreak. Exposure results in infection from an anomalous strain of Yersinia pestis resistant to all treatment. The mechanisms behind SCP-XXXX-1's antibiotic resistance are believed it be anomalous due to the lack of efflux pumps, drug-inactivating enzymes, or any other mechanism known to confer resistance.

Once the SCP is secured, the plot follows the project lead, Dr. Stephen Miller, in a vain attempt to neutralise the corpse due to the inherent risk of an XK-Class scenario if a containment breach were to occur. Unfortunately, his proposal is denied. He's given the usual spiel about how its a safe class object, how he'd be more at home at the Global Occult Coalition, about how historically attempted neutralisation of objects has often made things worse, which is why the Foundation contains rather than Destroy, Destroy, Destroy. The Site Director cites SCP-1609 as an example; it was a teleporting chair that the GOC put through a wood chipper. Now, it's a murderous pile of splinters.

What follows is a breach. An area of Site-19 becomes infected, and Beta-7 are deployed to clean up the mess, resulting in the death of Miller.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: We discover that SCP-1609 (and many others) are completely fabricated. They don't exist. They are nothing but Foundation propaganda, a way to convince Foundation personnel that the GOC are incompetent and the Foundations way is the correct way… the only way, to deal with the anomalous. Moreover, they serve as a warning to those who would try to preemptively neutralise an anomalous object. The breach was orchestrated by the O5s to kill Miller after discovering that he is a GOC mole.

item.title: SCP Idea: The Mechanical General
item.description: It's been a while, but I'm coming back with a new version of this SCP.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Drama, History
Page Layout: The page will have the basic SCP article layout, but with addendums sharing the development of the general’s story.
Elevator Pitch: A sapient Gundam model. Has organs underneath the plastic armor plates, but they do not match any living species. The model speaks in memories of a fallen Vietnam War general that seems to be from a different timeline.
Central Narrative: Tells the story of an American Vietnam War General. A Gundam model was found in a former Vietnamese battlefield with significant damage. On the surface, there is nothing particularly strange about it. However, there appear to be functioning organs beneath the plastic armor plates that do not match up to any known species. Although they appear to be human-like, they contain DNA that varies greatly from those of humans. The model cannot move, but it is known to speak. It speaks from the perspective of General Richard Hall. The story it tells starts on November 8, 1955, and ends on May 9, 1961. It starts with Richard Hall getting drafted into the army. The story from there consists mostly of him giving orders to other soldiers or dialogue from his side only. At any points in time where a bodily fluid would come out of a person, the same thing happens to the model. For instance, real tears come out when Richard Hall cries. Recorded excretions include tears, sweat, blood, and urine. The majority of soldiers that Hall orders do not have records of being in the military. Although the story encompasses almost seven years, the full seven years are not played out. Only select days are played out. These days include battles, significant interactions, and promotions. The full day is always played out. On the final day, there is a battle in which Hall fights. We can tell that many soldiers are dying. The last thing said every time is "What the hell is that?" before the model starts bleeding profusely. After the bleeding stops, the story stops completely, and the model becomes dormant for 214 hours. After this, the story begins again the exact same way, in a cyclical nature. The real Richard Hall was a major, not a general. He died on July 24, 2006. Something turned him into a Gundam, but it is unknown what.
Hook: Emotional story told by a Gundam model.

Page Type: SCP Article.

Genre: My design is meant to be spooky, but I may not achieve this factor.

Page Layout: The usual SCP statements, Item Name, Item Class but no picture. Information is going to be structured in the following layout; Appearance description (Height, weight, colour and shape), Discovery (How the anomaly was contained), Abilities (What the anomaly can do, how it does it etc) and the Addendums (Stories about previously explained things).

Elevator Pitch: The basic premise is a tall, slender, arctic hunter with elongated shoulder growths and large elbows, glowing crimson eyes, capable of seeing infrared radiation and heat signature, used for hunting. The anomaly has thousands of tiny muscles on its skin capable of moving guanine crystals to adjust the wavelength of light being reflected off the skin of the anomaly. This is commonly known as camouflage, and is the same method that the Chamaeleonidae (Common Chameleon) uses. Bone marrow scans and nervous axon scans have suggested that overgrowths on the anomaly's shoulder blades and elbows contain many nerve endings, which transfer electrical signals in large amounts to a particular area which creates an electromagnetic field. These electromagnetic pulses disrupt nearby local electric signals. It may use this to alter the function of electrical signals in the brain, or to inhibit power of technology.

– hide block

Central Narrative: It was a normal day in the UK Arctic Research Facility. It was collection day, where the scientific staff would take a collection of snow for carbon-testing, a process where the amount of carbon that is in a snowflake is collected. Suddenly, the power went out. As the staff stumbled over to the generator, senior researcher Noel Leon noticed a small red glow. Must have been nothing. He got back to fixing the generator and replaced the fuses. But as soon as the generator start-up was initiated, the generator failed. What was going on? Suddenly, pat… pat… pat…. He turned around, but there was nothing but footprints. SNAP. The crunch of his bones in SCP-XXXX's mouth was horrifying, but unheard to remaining staff. As it entered the facility, seven of it's prey had already been frozen. An easy meal. Junior researcher Doctor Edward turned a corner, but the anomaly was gone, just a frozen, half-eaten corpse. He was petrified, and sprinted out to the door and locked it shut. His frozen fingers dialled 911 into a telephone. The rest of the facility was wiped out, with the exception of Doctor Bradly who was obliterated by SCP-XXXX. Doctor Bradly called local authorities and the foundation was alerted. MTF unit Delta-92 Snow-and-Tell was sent to the situation immediately. Using infrared vision, the anomaly's ability was stunted, rendering it useless. Using a Class-3 collapsible containment cell, SCP-XXXX was taken to Site-25 via helicopter with ease.

item.title: Vision Says "No" (Seeking Greenlight)
item.description: An SCP that is impossible to look at. That's it.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is a human-like creature, around 6 feet tall. This is a SCP that is impossible to look at-not in the way of SCP-096 where if you look at its face, it will kill you, but as in the body will do everything it can to force a person not to look at it, e.g. making the person close their eyes, turning their head away, etc., similar to agnosia-this also effects photos and video recordings, not doing anything to alter them but still having the agnosia-type effect. The SCP is malevolent, and seems to be conscious of the effect it causes, as it constantly uses its inability to not be seen to anyone in the foundation to attempt escapes very frequently, making the containment not impossible, but very, very difficult.

Central Narrative: The foundation traces this SCP back to a road in an undisclosed town in Ohio, as specific section of the road had a sharp increase of traffic accidents for no apparent reason within 2-3 hours. After an investigative team gets there, they find nothing out of the ordinary except that they are physically unable to look down the center of the road. after pinpointing the center of the anomaly, they manage to find that the source of it is said SCP. The SCP goes along willingly, as this is its first encounter with the Foundation, but its anger towards them quickly ratchets up as strict containment procedures limit its freedom.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main hook of the story in my opinion is going to be mainly about the escape attempts of the SCP, as the foundation struggles to contain something impossible to look at and as the SCP finds new ways to trick the staff and exit, etc.

Additional Notes: This is not my first SCP Idea, but it is my first that I've gotten the courage to write up in here, so please tell me what is absolute garbage and what is ok

Once it has done this, if the higher value the number value displayed on the top of the dice, the higher level of damage the entity suffers. Tests show there is no way to cancel the anomalous effects and tests show the type of damage/death the entity suffers is also randomized. item.title: Killbox & Co.
item.description: A used car lot offering cars that kill their drivers.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Description with interviews and a mission log

Elevator Pitch: A used car lot in Colorado that offers dirt-cheap classic autos. All owners crash fatally after a week of driving.

Central Narrative:
+ My first custom block
- Are you proud of me ma

The Foundation notices an absurdly sharp increase in automotive-related deaths tracing back to a single car lot and, after some investigating, designate it an anomaly, including all staff. Interview logs with staff members. Staff members don't require sustenance and at 10 pm sharp are all in their predetermined spots, sleeping. The next day their memory is reset. When talked to, they generally behave like normal humans and show very strong devotion to the car lot.

Surveilance instated in a garage which provides the lot with its cars - proved futile as when a car appears, recording equipment malfunctions and witnesses black out. If anyone is seen approaching the garage, a staff member will warn them against it and become more and more agitated if subject doesn't move or refuse. Additionaly, other staff will begin to converge. If subject continues towards garage, staff will apprehend and throw them out. If subject gets into the garage, the salesman will say "Looks like the boss will take care of you now", upon which all exits to the garage close and Mr. Killbox enters the garage through a door leading to the main building. He is a 2.5 m brute with a mechanical arm made out of car parts. Shall the subject be caught, he will be killed and dragged behind the same door, which opens to an empty void for Killbox.

The staff will also start acting hostile if subject mentions Killbox by name or starts asking multiple questions in a row regarding the garage or the cars' origins.
Questions asked about the workers or the car lot will generally all result in answers like "The car lot is my life" and "I've worked here since as long as I can remember."
Staff have realistic human personalities, showing emotions and reacting as to be expected from regular humans. Their daily memory reset generally prevents them from developing critical thoughts. However, they are still capable of thinking freely (save for the instinctual response to trespassing into the garage).

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Final Destination-style elaborate death setups.

Additional Notes: Crashes aim to also kill bystanders. Spectacularly. Hence the death toll.
